chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Abu Zuhrah, from Umm al-Hasan al-Nakha'iyyah, who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) passed by me and said, 'What are you doing, O Umm al-Hasan?' I said, 'I am spinning [yarn].' He said, 'Indeed, it is the most permissible of earnings.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about the permissibility of manual labor like spinning?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Umm al-Hasan al-Nakha'iyyah underscores the Shia emphasis on the dignity of honest manual labor as a primary means of sustenance. Imam Ali’s designation of spinning as 'the most permissible of earnings' (*ahall al-kasb*) reflects the jurisprudential preference for self-sufficiency and the avoidance of dependency, a principle deeply rooted in the Prophet’s household's practice of engaging in trade and crafts.
